findings.description: No server_side_encryption_configuration block is defined, so objects in this bucket are stored without enforced encryption at rest.

findings.issue_category: no public access block / ACL restriction
findings.description: No bucket ACL is set explicitly and there is no aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block resource, leaving the bucket subject to default settings that could allow public access.
The bucket has acl set to private but no server_side_encryption_configuration, so financial ledger export data is stored unencrypted at rest.
Versioning and logging are configured but no server_side_encryption_configuration is present, leaving model artifacts unencrypted at rest.
No server_side_encryption_configuration block is defined for this bucket, so operational runbook data is stored without encryption at rest.

The acl value 'lcatalogopts-delivery-write' is not a valid S3 canned ACL; this looks like a typo for 'log-delivery-write' and, if applied, could fail or silently misconfigure access control for the audit log bucket, undermining its ability to receive/protect log deliveries as intended.
force_destroy = true allows the bucket and all its contents to be deleted without recoverability safeguards, increasing risk of accidental or malicious data loss for archived reports.
force_destroy = true permits deletion of a non-empty bucket containing ledger export data, risking irrecoverable loss of financial records.

findings.issue_category: force_destroy enabled on audit log bucket
findings.description: force_destroy = true on the audit trail bucket allows deletion of audit logs, undermining the integrity and availability guarantees expected of an audit logging store.

findings.issue_category: plaintext sensitive data upload without encryption enforcement
findings.description: The object is uploaded to a bucket lacking server-side encryption configuration and no server_side_encryption override is specified on the object itself, meaning potentially sensitive vendor roster data is stored unencrypted.
